subject: Private inference network & streaming: performance recap (ClearPath)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@clearpathhealth.com>, procurement@clearpathhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private inference network & streaming: performance recap (ClearPath)

Hi Eric / team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap + concrete asks so we have a single source of truth heading into the PoC window next week. I pasted the main points below; please flag anything I missed.

Summary of what ClearPath needs (from today's demo & call)
- Deployment mode: Private (VPC peering) to our on-prem inference gateway; customer will route egress through their managed peering connection.
- Expected concurrency: ~40 concurrent streaming sessions during peak (70% of traffic expected during weekday business hours).
- Streaming behavior: token-by-token streaming (server-sent events) for clinical note generation — first-token latency matters (cold start) and inter-token spacing matters for perceived throughput.
- Throughput baseline: nominally 800 tokens/sec sustained for the PoC traffic pattern; bursts up to 2,000 tokens/sec for short windows (<= 30s).
- Latency targets (goal): median first-byte <= 50ms, p95 first-byte <= 180ms, p99 <= 350ms for single-session streaming under expected network conditions.

Network / connectivity asks for the PoC
1) Provide a pair of representative public egress IPs we can expect to see from your peered gateway (for firewall allowlist).
2) Confirm whether your peering will NAT source IPs or preserve original source. If NAT-ing, please confirm NAT pool size and if ephemeral.
3) Run a traceroute (TCP) from the ClearPath gateway to our test endpoint and share results (we'll provide endpoint).
4) Allow us to run 10-minute sustained token generation tests during the agreed PoC slot; we will coordinate a specific time.
5) Can you share max MTU settings and any active traffic-shaping/QoS on the ClearPath egress path?

Technical details we covered
- We recommend keeping TLS over TCP for streaming and enabling keepalives to avoid cold TLS handshakes for long-running sessions.
- Redwood will enable KV-cache warmup prior to the test window for a subset of prompts to reduce first-token variance.

Next steps (owners)
- ClearPath: provide egress IPs, confirm NAT behavior, and share traceroute by EOD Tue (owner: Eric).
- Redwood (Karthik / Sergio): provide PoC test endpoints + a short test script and SLO matrix (owner: Karthik).
- Procurement: send the standard PO template and any additional security paperwork needed for Private deployments.

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO matrix and a short network playbook that we use for private PoCs.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

---
Attachment: clearpath_poc_slo-matrix.csv (stated contents: test cases, target p50/p95/p99, concurrency, tokens/sec)
Attachment: redwood_net_playbook.pdf (stated contents: peering checklist, sample iptables, MTU guidance)
From: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathhealth.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private inference network & streaming: performance recap (ClearPath)

Hi Camila —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:
1) Egress IPs: we run through a managed peering appliance; I can provide two egress IPs but they are behind a NAT pool — we will confirm whether we can reserve stable source IPs for the PoC.
2) MTU: our internal team reports 1450 on the peering appliance (we have PMTUD enabled).
3) QoS: we have priority class for clinical back-end traffic, but peering to external vendors is rate-limited to protect upstream; I need to confirm the exact burst window and rate cap.
4) Traceroute: we'll run tcp traceroute to your endpoint once you share it.

Two asks for Redwood: can Karthik and Sergio confirm the expected connection pattern (single persistent TLS connection per session vs multiple short-lived connections) and whether your test script will saturate multiple sessions from a single source IP? That matters because of our NAT behavior.

I'll get back with the egress IPs and NAT confirmation by Monday EOD. Procurement is looped for PO tracking — procurement@clearpathhealth.com.

Thanks,
Eric Barnes
Head of Infrastructure, ClearPath Health
eric.barnes@clearpathhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@clearpathhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private inference network & streaming: performance recap (ClearPath)

Hi Eric / Camila —

Thanks — below are the concrete technical details and a short PoC test plan. We kept the targets conservative for the PoC so we can iterate after the first run.

Redwood test plan (high level)
- PoC window: 60 minutes (planned): 10m ramp, 40m steady-state, 10m cool-down.
- Client pattern: 40 concurrent streaming sessions (each session opens one persistent TLS connection and streams tokens using SSE/gRPC chunking).
- Traffic origin: for the first run we will originate all sessions from a single test host behind the customer NAT to mirror production. We will note concurrent source IPs in results and can run a second test with distributed sources if NAT causes head-of-line limits.

SLOs (PoC acceptance criteria - initial)
- First-byte (first token) latency: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 350ms
- Inter-token spacing (steady-state): median <= 20ms, p95 <= 75ms (this is measured on the client side for streaming gaps)
- Throughput: sustain 800 tokens/sec for 40 sessions (aggregate), tolerate bursts to 2,000 tokens/sec for <= 30s with <5% error rate
- Error rate: <1.5% HTTP/gRPC error responses during steady-state

Network measurements we need from ClearPath (deliverables)
1) TCP traceroute (Paris traceroute if available) to redwood-poc-us-west-1.redwood.com:443 during a quiet period and during a test run (we'd like both).
2) Sample tcpdump (10s) from your gateway showing a single session TLS handshake and first 2 streaming packets (we need to confirm obfuscation/PII before sharing).
3) Confirmation whether NAT source IPs rotate at sub-minute granularity; if so we will request a NAT-exempt range for the test host.

Endpoint & test script
- Redwood will provide: redwood-poc-us-west-1.redwood.com:443 and a small curl/node script that opens N persistent SSE connections and streams token payloads with timestamps. The script will publish a CSV of per-token latencies so you can cross-check on your side.

If all of the above is acceptable, next actions:
- Eric: share egress IP(s) + NAT behavior + traceroute results (owner: Eric)
- Camila: confirm PoC schedule (owner: Camila)
- Karthik/Sergio: deliver test endpoints + test script by Mon EOD PT (owner: Karthik)

Notes: if the NAT prevents sustaining 40 concurrent distinct source sockets, we can run the test with distributed agents (we can spin additional test hosts) but we wanted to test the simplest integration first.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
